```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# load most recent County Health Rankings data
chr2025_raw <- read.csv("analytic_data2025.csv") # data from 2022
sup2026_raw <- read.csv("analytic_supplement_20260325.csv") # data from 2023

chr2025 <- chr2025_raw |>
  select(
    fips = County.FIPS.Code,
    name = Name, 
    state = State.Abbreviation,
    state_fips = State.FIPS.Code,
    release_year = Release.Year,
    flu_vac = Flu.Vaccinations.raw.value,
    pcp_ratio = Ratio.of.population.to.primary.care.physicians.,
    pcp_raw = Primary.Care.Physicians.raw.value,
    rural = X..Rural.raw.value,
    income = Median.Household.Income.raw.value,
    uninsured_adults = Uninsured.Adults.raw.value,
    uninsured_children = Uninsured.Children.raw.value,
    hs_comp = High.School.Completion.raw.value,
    some_college = Some.College.raw.value,
    Non_Proficient_English = X..Not.Proficient.in.English.raw.value
  ) |>
  filter(fips != 0) |>
  mutate(fips = as.numeric(fips)) |>
  as_tibble()

# gather more recent variables when they exist (mapping done per codebook)
sup2026 <- sup2026_raw |>
  select(
    fips = countycode,
    name = county, 
    state,
    state_fips = statecode,
    flu_vac = v155_rawvalue,
    pcp_ratio = v004_rawalternatevalue,
    pcp_raw = v004_rawvalue,
    uninsured_adults = v003_rawvalue,
    uninsured_children = v122_rawvalue
  ) |>
  mutate(release_year = "2026") |>
  filter(fips != 0) |>
  as_tibble()

head(chr2025)
head(sup2026)
```
We have observations for n=3152 counties.

# Outcome variable: vaccination rate

Ideally, we want to use the vaccination rate at the county level from the supplemental data for 2023, released in 2026, as it is the most recent. First we will compare the vaccination rates from 2022 and 2023.

```{r}
#| eval: true
summary(chr2025$flu_vac)
summary(sup2026$flu_vac)

hist(chr2025$flu_vac)
hist(sup2026$flu_vac)
```

The vaccination rate is higher in 2022. The distribution for 2023 is fairly symmetric where as the distribution for 2022 is a bit more left skewed. 

Next, we will compare missingness.
```{r}
sum(is.na(chr2025$flu_vac))
sum(is.na(sup2026$flu_vac))
round(sum(is.na(sup2026$flu_vac))/nrow(sup2026), 4)
```

Just under 1% of the data is missing for flu_vac overall in the 2026 data and only a few more counties for 2026 compared, so it is acceptable to use the outcome from the 2026 supplemental data.

```{r}
# Join to create one data set, excluding counties with no data for 2023 flu vaccination rate.
full_data <- 
  left_join(sup2026, chr2025, 
            by=c("fips", "state_fips", "name", "state"), suffix = c(".23",".22")) |> 
  #select(-ends_with(".y")) |> # Remove 2025 columns when we have 2026 data
  #rename_with(~gsub("\\.x$", "", .)) |> # Remove .x suffix from 2026 columns
  filter(!is.na(flu_vac.23)) |> # Exclude counties with no data for 2023 flu vaccination rate.
  select(-flu_vac.22, flu_vac = flu_vac.23)

chr2025 <- chr2025 |> filter(!is.na(flu_vac))
sup2026 <- sup2026 |> filter(!is.na(flu_vac))

final_data <- full_data
```

# PCP Ratio
```{r}
# Missingness
#summary(chr2025$pcp_ratio) # 154 NAs
#summary(sup2026$pcp_ratio) # 243 NAs
#nrow(full_data |> filter(is.na(coalesce(pcp_ratio.23, pcp_ratio.22)))) # 147 NAs

# Conclusion: 2025 is more complete and there are only 7 extra counties we drop by using 2025 only, this is acceptable

#hist(final_data$pcp_ratio.22) # right skewed
# When there are 0 providers in a county, pcp = -population 
#nrow(final_data |> filter(pcp_ratio.22 < 0)) # 68 rows < 0

final_data <- full_data |> filter(!is.na(pcp_ratio.22) & pcp_ratio.22 >= 0) |>
  select(-pcp_ratio.23, pcp_ratio = pcp_ratio.22)

summary(final_data$pcp_ratio) # median pcp ratio is 2100 patients per provider
hist(final_data$pcp_ratio) # right-skewed
hist(log(final_data$pcp_ratio))
ggplot(final_data, aes(pcp_ratio, flu_vac)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .5) + 
  labs (
    title = "2023 Flu Vaccination Rate vs 2022 PCP Ratio",
    x = "Population/Primary Care Physicians",
    y = "Flu Vaccination rate") +
  geom_smooth(method=lm)

```

# % Rural
Only available in the 2025 release.
```{r}
# Missingness
summary(chr2025$rural) # 8 NAs, acceptable
final_data <- final_data |> filter(!is.na(rural))

# Distribution
hist(final_data$rural) # left-skewed with many counties 100% rural

ggplot(final_data, aes(x = jitter(rural, amount = .02), y = flu_vac)) +
  geom_point() + labs (
    title = "County 2022 Rural % vs 2023 Flu Vaccination Rate",
    x = "Rural %",
    y = "Flu Vaccination rate"
  )
```

# Modeling Plan: 
Income, uninsured rates and education exploratory plots showed possible relationship with flu vaccination rates. Non-Proficiency in English rate we did not see a relationship. For education and uninsured rates we need to be careful within both of them for colinearty so we may decide to only look at variable within both of them (for example just looking at uninsured adults and some_college).
